text:
alex: Heads up — saw a spike in ECC correctable alerts from DCGM exporter in usw2 last night. ~30 nodes flared with short-lived bursts, lots of noise; 3 alerts/hour for the same card. Thinking we should stop firing on single-event thresholds and move to an aggregation/weighting rule (streak scoring + decay) so noisy cards don't keep paging people. Thoughts?

ben: +1 to weighting. We did something similar for disk SMART flaps. Proposal: assign weights (uncorrectable=5, correctable=1, xid=2) and compute a rolling score per GPU with a 1h decay. Fire only if score>6.

sophia: That sounds reasonable. How would you implement in Prom rules? We should be careful with latency-sensitive workloads — draining too aggressively hurts production. Also make sure the rule keeps card-level granularity (not node aggregate).

ben: Example recording + alert rule (rough sketch):
```yaml
# recording rule: per-gpu score over 1h with 15m decay window
- record: gpu:errant_score:1h
  expr: |
    sum_over_time(
      (dcgm_gpu_ecc_uncorrectable{job="dcgm"} * 5)
      + (dcgm_gpu_ecc_correctable{job="dcgm"} * 1)
      + (dcgm_gpu_xid_errors_total{job="dcgm"} * 2)
    )[1h:1m]
    by (node, gpu_index)

# alert: only fire when score > 6 for 20m
- alert: GPUErrantCardHighScore
  expr: gpu:errant_score:1h > 6
  for: 20m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU {{ $labels.node }}/gpu{{ $labels.gpu_index }} errant score high"
```

ben: That avoids single blips and weights uncorrectable heavily.

alex: Nice. Two questions: 1) should we add a cooldown per-card (suppress repeats for 6h after a page)? 2) can we route severity based on whether the card is in Dedicated customer pools vs shared fleet?

sophia: For cooldown we can use silence/auto-snooze in Alertmanager for 6h on that fingerprint, but we should keep an internal metric when a card was last remediated so we don't mask a real wear-out pattern. Maybe add a separate rule for "score growth rate" to bypass cooldown if score keeps rising quickly.

lina: For routing: label nodes with pool type (pool=dedi/shared) at scrape time, then Alertmanager routes pages for dedicated pools to infra-critical, others to infra-low with oncall escalation only if multiple cards on a node exceed threshold. Keeps customers from seeing noisy pages.

alex: Good call on scrape labels. Also want to include a small whitelist for known noisy cards (lab GPUs) to exclude from paging while we repro. Keep the alert still recorded for telemetry.

infra-bot: deploybot: alertmanager config change staged to canary; no pages yet. :robot_face:

ben: One more edge case: MIG devices. Need to roll up by MIG instance id or map to parent GPU. Use dcgm labels (mig_instance) if present, else fallback to gpu_index.

sophia: Agreed. I'll open a tiny PR with the recording rule + alert tweak and a short runbook: how to triage (check NVME logs, pci errors, kernel XIDs, escalate to RMA). Will include the suppression/cooldown knobs in alertmanager.

alex: Thanks — please cc eng-sre and eng-oncall in the PR. If we can get the canary in us-west-2 tonight that'd be great.

lina: I'll add the pool label mapping and a separate route for dedicated pools.

ben: TL;DR: move to weighted rolling-score rule, 20m for alert, 6h cooldown via silence, special routes for dedicated vs shared, keep recording rules for telemetry and rate-of-change bypass.

alex: Sounds like a plan.
